newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to ease controls on fund managing firms.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to ease controls on fund managing firms.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Monday it would allow domestic fund managing companies to invest less of their assets in stocks to help improve their business.
A ministry official said the 18 local firms would be required to invest a minimum of 20 percent of their assets in stocks, compared with a minimum of 50 percent at present.
He said the firms had difficulty selling products under current rules due to the sluggish stock market.
The eased regulation will take effect upon approval from the Minister of Finance and Economy, he said.
